title: Introduce orthogonal cache coalescer and incremental sparse index to reduce pagination tail latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: On heavy tenant workloads we observe 99.9th-percentile pagination tail latency spikes when users traverse deep cursors or switch query facets. Root causes we traced: 1) many small misses in cold prefix caches that cause multiple serialized backend fetches; 2) high variance in shard response times causing long-tail latencies; 3) duplicated work across concurrently-issued nearby cursor windows.

Proposal: Build an "orthogonal cache coalescer" layer in the console query API stack plus an incremental sparse index materializer. The coalescer sits between request routing and shard fetch logic and implements: 
- probabilistic request grouping for near-identical cursor windows to deduplicate backend work;
- hedged/parallelized fetches for high-variance shards when a soft latency threshold is crossed;
- adaptive prefetching of the next N cursor blocks using a low-cost sparse index snapshot to avoid synchronous cold reads.

The incremental sparse index component maintains compact per-tenant anchor points (every K entries) and a tiny bloom-filter-like summary for each shard window so prefetches are high-precision and low-cost. Index updates are append-only and materialized asynchronously (small background writer) to keep writes cheap.

Why different from prior work: we avoid heavy full-materialized cursors or large in-memory caches. Instead we target orthogonal dimensions: coalescing concurrent requests (horizontal dedupe), small precise prefetches (vertical hinting), and hedged fetches (tail mitigation). This should reduce both median and 99.9th tail for deep pagination without blowing memory or write amplification.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind "coalescer-v1" with tunables: grouping window (ms), prefetch depth (blocks), sparse index cadence (K), hedge threshold (ms). Start with 10% of tenants (randomized by tenant hash), instrument detailed telemetry, compare baseline and treatment across: p50/p95/p99/p999 latency, tokens-per-query cost, backend request count, and cache hit rate.

Metrics target: reduce p999 pagination latency by >=30% for affected queries while increasing backend request volume by <10% and memory overhead <5% per node.
acceptance_criteria: Feature flag gating and config surface in console config store
Unit and integration tests covering coalescing logic, hedged fetch path, and prefetch behavior
Perf benchmark harness showing p999 reduction >=30% on synthetic tenant workloads
Telemetry dashboards added: coalescer_hits, grouped_requests, hedged_fetch_count, sparse_index_prefetch_precision
Gradual rollout plan documented with rollback triggers (error rate increase, cost drift >20%, median latency regression)
steps: Design doc: consolidate algorithms and tunables (link below)
Implement orthogonal coalescer middleware in query gateway (golang)
Add sparse index writer/reader (compact proto + append-only segments)
Integrate hedged fetch logic with existing shard client and implement timeout/abort semantics
Add feature flag and runtime config in console control plane
End-to-end tests + load tests in staging, iterate on thresholds
Gradual rollout to 10% -> 30% -> 100% with throttles and rollback hooks
